- Presence across electrical infrastructure activities with major revenue from O&M services, spanning three service verticals (O&M 76.90% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026)
- Order book providing revenue visibility - 34 ongoing projects with unexecuted value of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores as of June 30, 2026, primarily from electricity distribution utilities
- Majority of revenue from repetitive customers - 88.29% in FY 2025-26, 97.14% in FY 2024-25 and 99.28% in FY 2023-24
- Experienced management team and manpower strength - 4,473 employees as of May 31, 2026 (4,332 permanent and 141 contractual), led by two promoter-directors each with over 30 years of experience
- Recurring/periodic billing under annual maintenance contracts and rate contracts, as compared to project-based execution, providing revenue visibility over the contract duration
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer-segment concentration on power distribution utilities — A major portion of revenue is derived from electricity distribution utilities (79.10% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, 88.73% in Fiscal 2025, 88.87% in Fiscal 2024); any reduction in business from such customers, adverse changes in procurement practices or failure to secure new contracts may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows
- Dependence on sector capital expenditure, government policy and schemes such as RDSS — Demand for the Company's services is directly linked to the level of investment in electricity distribution infrastructure, which is influenced by capital expenditure programmes of utilities, availability of funding, government policies and reforms, and implementation of sectoral schemes such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme
- Regulated counterparties with constrained financial position and investment capacity — Electricity distribution utilities operate within a regulated framework and are subject to approval processes and performance requirements prescribed by regulatory authorities; their financial position and investment capacity affect the Company
- Order book conversion risk — Realization of revenues from the order book of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores is subject to commencement and progress of projects, issuance of work orders, site availability, customer approvals and other factors beyond the Company's control; there can be no assurance the entire order book will convert into revenue within expected timelines or at all
- Geographic concentration — Odisha contributed 69.05%, 74.52% and 67.09% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively, leaving revenue exposed to a single state's distribution capex and tendering
- Dependence on competitive tendering and repeat orders — Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender processes; ability to continue receiving repeat orders depends on performance of existing contracts, customer requirements, competitive bidding and other external factors, and repeat-customer revenue share has declined from 99.28% (FY 2023-24) to 88.29% (FY 2025-26)
- Manpower-intensive operations in high-voltage environments — Execution depends on deployment of a 4,473-person workforce (as of May 31, 2026) of supervisors, linemen, technicians and helpers across designated service areas, supported by vehicles, tools and equipment, with defined operating procedures required for high-voltage work

business.body: The Company provides operation, maintenance and field-level execution of works relating to electricity distribution networks and associated infrastructure, including distribution lines, feeders, substations, poles and cables. Operations are organised into three service verticals: Network O&M Services, Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works, and Metering and Meter Management Services. Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tenders by electricity distribution utilities under rate contracts, outline agreements or annual maintenance contracts, with work orders issued from time to time; private sector clients may award work directly.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company provides operation, maintenance and field-level execution of works relating to electricity distribution networks and associated infrastructure, including distribution lines, feeders, substations, poles and cables. Operations are organised into three service verticals: Network O&M Services, Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works, and Metering and Meter Management Services. risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer-segment concentration on power distribution utilities — A major portion of revenue is derived from electricity distribution utilities (79.10% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, 88.73% in Fiscal 2025, 88.87% in Fiscal 2024); any reduction in business from such customers, adverse changes in procurement practices or failure to secure new contracts may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows
- Dependence on sector capital expenditure, government policy and schemes such as RDSS — Demand for the Company's services is directly linked to the level of investment in electricity distribution infrastructure, which is influenced by capital expenditure programmes of utilities, availability of funding, government policies and reforms, and implementation of sectoral schemes such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme
- Regulated counterparties with constrained financial position and investment capacity — Electricity distribution utilities operate within a regulated framework and are subject to approval processes and performance requirements prescribed by regulatory authorities; their financial position and investment capacity affect the Company
- Order book conversion risk — Realization of revenues from the order book of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores is subject to commencement and progress of projects, issuance of work orders, site availability, customer approvals and other factors beyond the Company's control; there can be no assurance the entire order book will convert into revenue within expected timelines or at all
- Geographic concentration — Odisha contributed 69.05%, 74.52% and 67.09% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively, leaving revenue exposed to a single state's distribution capex and tendering
- Dependence on competitive tendering and repeat orders — Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender processes; ability to continue receiving repeat orders depends on performance of existing contracts, customer requirements, competitive bidding and other external factors, and repeat-customer revenue share has declined from 99.28% (FY 2023-24) to 88.29% (FY 2025-26)
- Manpower-intensive operations in high-voltage environments — Execution depends on deployment of a 4,473-person workforce (as of May 31, 2026) of supervisors, linemen, technicians and helpers across designated service areas, supported by vehicles, tools and equipment, with defined operating procedures required for high-voltage work
